title: How Guilty Gear Achieves its 2D Look

format.seo_title: How Guilty Gear Achieves its 2D Look
format.seo_description: Arc System Works spent years developing the Guilty Gear look. There are so many big and small techniques that create this style that it's almost impossible to identify them all. Luckily for us, ASW have actually published a lot of resources explaining how they have done it. On this page I'll try to explain the techniques and methods they use as clearly as possible and how you can apply them in your own projects.

Made by Noggi from YouTube.
Here you’ll find all the resource pages I have shared so far in my videos and elsewhere.

title: Every surface in 3D has a direction it's pointing in. Take a flat plane: you can describe which way it faces by drawing a line sticking straight out of it. That line is called a normal.

i.c: Every surface in 3D has a direction it's pointing in. Take a flat plane: you can describe which way it faces by drawing a line sticking straight out of it. That line is called a normal.

title: A 3D model is made up of many of these planes combined together. Each one has its own normal, and the 3D software calculates them automatically. But you can also edit them manually to create various different effects. Some of them are being covered later.

i.c: A 3D model is made up of many of these planes combined together. Each one has its own normal, and the 3D software calculates them automatically. But you can also edit them manually to create various different effects. Some of them are being covered later.

title: Standard 3D shading creates a smooth gradient from lit to dark across every surface. That gradient is what makes things read as three-dimensional. A cel shader on the other hand, limits the shading to one light and one dark color and three things determine what parts of the model are lit or unlit.

title: If you’re looking at a subject from a certain angle a rim light is placed on the opposite side of that subject. If you’re looking from the front, the rim light will be placed at the back. Its purpose is to illuminate the edges of the subject, to separate it from the background and clarify its shape. ASW added rim lights to the Guilty Gear characters as well.

title: Shadows in 3D anime fall into two types.

i.c: Shadows in 3D anime fall into two types.

title: Self-shadows
b

are cast by one part of the character onto another. The most common case is a big hairstyle dropping an enormous dark patch across the neck and shoulders. These vary a lot depending on the character’s design and are hard to control.

i.c: are cast by one part of the character onto another. The most common case is a big hairstyle dropping an enormous dark patch across the neck and shoulders. These vary a lot depending on the character’s design and are hard to control.

title: Drop shadows
b
are cast onto the ground. These can help integrate the character in the environment and are much easier to control.

i.c: are cast onto the ground. These can help integrate the character in the environment and are much easier to control.

title: Their solution is simple: Disable self-shadows, keep drop shadows. The result isn't perfect, but it's predictable. And predictable is something you can work with.

title: The basic cel shader treats the threshold as a single value across the entire character. That works, but most of the time you’ll notice that the lighting is not perfect by default. Some areas are lit, even though they should be in shadow.

title: This is because the dot product shader does not calculate drop shadows, meaning shadows created where one surface blocks the light from hitting another surface behind it.
